image_description: A close-up, front-facing view of a single circular loudspeaker driver (woofer) with a grey metallic frame and cone. The image shows the central dust cap, the conical diaphragm, and the mounting flange with screw holes. There is no visible enclosure, tweeter, or rear panel.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight crop of a driver unit; the surrounding enclosure is completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: One or more circular speaker cones on front face of varying sizes.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A single circular speaker cone is clearly visible and dominates the image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Prominent large woofer dominating the front face with a much smaller tweeter positioned above or beside it.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only one driver is visible. A tweeter cannot be seen due to the cropping/framing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Cone surface made of paper, polypropylene, or composite with rubber surround.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The texture appears consistent with treated paper or composite material, and a flexible surround is visible at the outer edge of the cone.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Grille cloth or perforated metal may cover the drivers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The driver is exposed; there is no grille covering it.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Terminal connections visible on rear panel.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows only the front face; the rear panel is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wood, MDF, or plastic enclosure with black, white, or wood-grain finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No enclosure material is visible in the frame.
The object is visually identifiable as a standard dynamic speaker driver.
Functionally correct identification based on visual features.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The gradient shading on the cone is extremely smooth and uniform, lacking the subtle micro-texture or fiber details typically seen in real paper/polypropylene cones under close inspection. It has a slight 'airbrushed' AI look.

The screw holes on the outer rim are inconsistent. Some appear as dark voids, while others are shallow grey smudges. They lack the precise mechanical depth and sharp edges of a manufactured metal stamping.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of audio component and rule out misclassification as a generic wheel or mechanical part.
To check for edge bleeding between the cone and the frame, and ensure the circular geometry is mathematically perfect without warping.
To assess the realism of the lighting reflections on the metal frame and the plausibility of the shadows within the screw holes.

focus_areas: Consistency of screw hole depth and shape
Texture realism of the cone material
Lighting coherence on the metallic rim
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the screw holes on the perimeter. In AI images, these often melt or vary in shape. Also, verify if the concentric circles of the speaker cone share a perfect center point, as AI often drifts slightly off-center.
